actions.reason: A block does not yield an observed revenue amount.
Tracking is an audience-data rights action and does not establish payment.
Ads can run for the rightsholder and sometimes be shared with the uploader; no rate is disclosed.

rules: Content ID tracking, monetization and blocking are claim-policy actions, not separate verified financial transfers.
An uploader can share rights revenue only when an applicable authorized arrangement permits it; never assume a contractual percentage.
If the original dispute is filed no later than the fifth calendar day after claim placement, held revenue begins on the claim day; filing later means holding from dispute filing.
Held during dispute does not mean creator-owned money, a bank deposit, realized loss or automatic entitlement to the gross advertising amount.
If the claim remains unchallenged, YouTube describes a five-day release-to-claimant rule for held revenues; this is not proof of any particular creator's earnings.
Content ID claims and formal copyright removal notices/strikes are distinct and can have different appeal and legal consequences.
Claim policy may differ across territories. A single country observation cannot establish worldwide lost views or payouts.
Do not infer payment amount, creator profit, actual license pricing, tax obligations, legal fees, or opportunity cost from documented procedures.
